predecessors.name: Kingdom of Prussia
predecessors.text: the Prussian Altmark and Magdeburg west of the Elbe, with Halberstadt, Hildesheim, Quedlinburg, Minden, Paderborn and other lands ceded by Prussia at Tilsit

predecessors.name: Electorate of Hesse
predecessors.text: Hesse-Cassel (with Schaumburg, excluding Hanau, Schmalkalden and Katzenelnbogen)

predecessors.name: County of Stolberg
predecessors.text: the county of Stolberg ('The counties of Mansfeld, Stolberg, Ravensberg, Rietberg and Hohnstein')

successors.name: Kingdom of Prussia
successors.text: most territories became Prussian in 1815; the counties of Rietberg and Stolberg-Wernigerode were annexed by Prussia

successors.name: Electorate of Hesse
successors.text: Hesse-Cassel, restored with 'the status quo of 1806'

successors.name: Duchy of Brunswick
successors.text: Brunswick-Wolfenbüttel, restored with the 1806 status quo

successors.name: Kingdom of Hanover
successors.text: Göttingen, Grubenhagen and Osnabrück, restored with the 1806 status quo

ledger.x: 1807: Napoleon makes his brother Jérôme king of the new Kingdom of Westphalia at Cassel.
1807: Prussian lands west of the Elbe ceded at Tilsit form the core of Westphalia.
1807: Hesse-Cassel is absorbed into Westphalia, which takes its capital Cassel; the Hanau, Schmalkalden and Katzenelnbogen parts stay outside.
1807: Brunswick-Wolfenbüttel, listed among the original territories, becomes the Oker department.
1807: Göttingen and Grubenhagen (the Leine department) and Osnabrück are in the kingdom from its creation.
1807: the county of Stolberg is among the original territories of the kingdom. county-of-stolberg /ledger/8 dissolves into Westphalia in 1807.
1807: Westphalia is a client state of France from its creation.

1810: the Aller department (capital Hanover) appears in the page's department table for 1810-1813, and the page says that in December 1810 'the short-lived coastal and northern départements Nord... and Niederelbe... were ceded to the French Empire', so the kingdom held Nord and Niederelbe before that month.
1810: the Weser department (Osnabrück) is listed as lasting only 1807-1810.
December 1810: 'the short-lived coastal and northern départements Nord... and Niederelbe... were ceded to the French Empire.'
September 1813: the Russian general Chernyshyov seizes Cassel in a night raid and Jérôme flees; the French retake the city on 7 October.
26 October 1813: after the French defeat at Leipzig (19 October) Prussian troops occupy Westphalia; the fighting over the kingdom ends with its dissolution.
26 October 1813: the client state ends with the kingdom.

26 October 1813: the Kingdom of Westphalia is dissolved after Leipzig and its lands revert to the 1806 status quo; most pass to Prussia in 1815 and Rietberg and Stolberg-Wernigerode are annexed by Prussia.

wars.name: War of the Sixth Coalition
wars.outcome: Chernyshyov took Cassel on 28-29 September 1813, the French retook it on 7 October, and after Leipzig (19 October) Prussian troops occupied Westphalia on 26 October; the kingdom was dissolved and the 1806 status quo restored.

certainty.note: The page lists the departments and their capitals but no boundary survey; the outline rests on Cliopatria's approximation.
